steps.content: Two days ago.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...So that's what we're dealing with. Echo doesn't believe she's tone-deaf and is refusing treatment.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Therefore, I want to use concert practice as an excuse, and hope you can try to correct some of her issues.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: What does she think about it?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Echo takes her performance very seriously. She agreed as soon as she heard it's for the concert.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: Alright, nothing difficult if it's just practice sessions.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: I won't ask for much, the tuition fee is 100,000 DisCoins, paid in one lump sum. What do you say, Chief?

steps.speaker: Peggy
steps.content: Ha! No problem, count on me!
It's been two days since you entrusted Echo to those three musicians.
Today, you finally manage to get away from your busy duties and plan to check on them.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: A rapper, a rock star, a folk musician...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: With those three training her, it should be fine, right...
Wooooo!
However, the reality, despite Echo's denial, is much more brutal than imagined.
A strange, loud noise almost ruptures your eardrums. You rush over immediately and push the door open.

steps.speaker: Peggy
steps.content: Finally, you're here!
Peggy pulls you aside with lightning speed, followed closely by Joan and Dudu.
And you notice that Echo is playing the saxophone with her eyes closed, completely engrossed. The terrifying sound just now came from that brass instrument.

steps.speaker: Peggy
steps.content: I'm telling you, this is much more serious than what you told us!

steps.speaker: Peggy
steps.content: Are you sure you want her to play at that concert? For real?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: I demand injury compensation!

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Every day I head back, I almost forget how to play my suona. As soon as I pick it up, I feel a buzzing in my head.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: Echo's pitch is terrible, she's always out of tune.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: I played the guitar better than her when I was three!
It's clear that everyone has been tormented by Echo's "demonic sound." They complain to you one after another, and you can only smile apologetically.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Thanks for your hard work, really! I wouldn't know what to do without you all...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So, how's the rehearsal going...?

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: ...There's still some progress, I guess.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: Echo's memory is not bad. Apart from the music scores, she can remember every fingering and skill that has been demonstrated to her.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: But correcting movements doesn't ensure the pitch is accurate...
Dudu adds in a melancholic tone.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: A wind instrument player also needs to pay attention to lip control and breathing rhythm, which is hard for people with a poor sense of pitch to learn by listening.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: So we can only ask Echo to play over and over again, and we listen and correct her errors so that she memorizes the correct playing method. Although she has improved, but meanwhile...

steps.speaker: Peggy
steps.content: Our ears and mental health have suffered immensely!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I know it's not easy for you guys... Don't worry! I'll do my best to fulfill the requests you mentioned before!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Whether it's Peggy's equipment, Joan's new album, or... Dudu's injury compensation, I'll fight for it!
After your reassurance and a series of promises, the trio finally look much less resentful.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: ...Let's make it clear, Chief.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: This training method can only allow Echo to barely play these few pieces correctly. It's not helping her amusia at all.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: For now, it's good enough. Let's just get through that concert first, it's fine as long as she doesn't continue to spread Mania to the general public with her noise.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We'll talk about the treatment later.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Well then! Now...

steps.speaker: Peggy
steps.content: You must stay here with us!!!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Alright, alright...
Being held "hostage," you have no choice but to stay and experience this "captivating and bewitching melody."
Even so, you still feel a sense of relief in this situation—After all, Echo's performance has indeed improved. She sounds much better than before.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Thank goodness, there's still hope.
When Echo sees you, she excitedly raises her saxophone. You respond with an encouraging smile, and she plays even more passionately.
For the next few hours, you keep on smiling until your facial muscles are about to go stiff. Although you don't give anything away, you fully understand the pain of Dudu and the others.
The three who have been tortured all day can't endure like you anymore, their faces looking even worse than before—they're barely holding on.
You immediately stand up and clap your hands.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's it for today! Joan, Dudu, Peggy, thank you, head back and get some rest!
The three let out a sigh of relief. They rush out the door one after another, not willing to stay a moment longer.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You did well too, Echo. Now, maybe we can start designing the stage for the performance?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Stage design is also a part of the performance, right?

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Of course, you always think of everything, Chief.
After wiping her saxophone, Echo carefully puts it away, then enthusiastically takes out a variety of strange props and decorations.
The props are a mix of everything, old, chipped, ruggedly shaped, you name it. But they're all very clean, clearly well cared for by their owner.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: I got these ribbons from a bakery owner. She had some extra left from packing her cakes. I scraped off the cream on them, tasted pretty good!

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: These balloons were from a school's art festival. I deflated them and smuggled them out before the cleaners arrived!

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: And these were picks left behind by street bands, I strung them together. Usually, when a show ends, many picks are left on the ground...

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Oh, right, how could I forget my favorite teddy bear and drumming monkey! They were thank-you gifts I received for helping a toy store owner move his storage all day!

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Look at this monkey, I heard it used to move... What a pity, if it wasn't broken, it could have joined my performance.
Echo vividly recounts the stories behind each prop. It seems, to her, they aren't just trash picked up from the streets, but rare and precious gifts in her life.
Then, she picks up a few pages of torn sheet music, carefully cradling them in front of her chest, her face beaming with joy.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: I really wish I could have a perfect, awe-inspiring performance just like those legendary bands...

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: The audience would applaud me, cheer for me, and praise the saxophone as the most charming instrument in the world!

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Most importantly, if they acknowledge me, they will feel the power of the saxophone music—the music that gives me strength and hope in the coldest winter nights!
Her expression becomes very serious, as if she's declaring some grand ambition.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Why "the coldest winter nights" specifically?

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Because... Eastside's winters are very cold, especially at night. It feels like a bunch of needles hitting your bones when the wind blows your way.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: The underpass is a great spot to hide from the cold. Last year, I had my eye on one for the winter since autumn, but another group of people took over my "home" and forced me out onto the streets...

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: It was a holiday that day, every house was warmly lit... but not a single door, not a single light belonged to me.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: I was cold and hungry, and when I felt like I couldn't hold on any longer, I heard an incredibly beautiful melody in my daze...
The moment she mentions that "beautiful melody," a smile of bliss emerges on Echo's face.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: I followed the sound to the brightest spot on the street, which seemed to be a theater with many people singing and dancing inside.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: But I didn't care about that, I pressed my face against the window, wanting to listen carefully to that dreamy and gentle melody...

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Finally, I heard it clearly, a warm, enchanting sound...!

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: As I listened, the cold and hunger were gone, and my body was once again filled with inexhaustible strength!
She clenches her fists, her eyes shining, and yells excitedly:

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: It was like a miracle!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's... quite an amazing experience...

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Yes! So I believed that was a form of art, a very noble and sacred one!

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: After the melody ended, people came out from the theatre. I grabbed them and asked what that music was, and a kind person told me, it was saxophone!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Wait, the saxophone piece during the theatre's closing...
You recall your experience at the Fortuna Theater and instantly understand what Echo had heard.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Is something wrong?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...No, nothing. So, after that, you fell in love with saxophone?

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Yeah! I was super lucky. I found a saxophone in a discarded box by the theatre's door, and that became my Kute! It's old, but in good condition, and can play great tunes.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: I even found a few saxophone textbooks and sheet music next to it! Hehe, I, Echo, the once-in-a-century musical genius just read those books once, and completely mastered it!

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: And I decided, I want to become a legendary saxophonist, and perform for everyone around the world, connecting with them and touching their heart with my music!

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: This is my lifelong mission!
Echo dramatically spreads her arms wide and lifts her head, lost in her overwhelming emotions.
You have to admit, disregarding her actual playing level, this is indeed an inspiring and touching fairytale-like story.
A warmth fills your chest, you can't help but be moved by her passion. You probably understand why being a "genius saxophonist" is such an important thing to her...
Saxophone and music have become the reason for Echo to keep going. Therefore, she refuses to admit that she has a condition that might stop her from achieving this "perfect goal."
If she admits it, that means she has to give up her dream, and her ideal life.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...I didn't know you have such a big ambition.
You pat Echo's head, and give her a thumbs-up.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: In that case, you need to keep practicing. I heard from Dudu and the others that there is a lot you need to improve on in your performance.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: I know! I'll give my best!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I believe that as long as you keep working hard, you'll be able to play the best music at the concert.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: That's what I've been saying. You just didn't believe me!

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: In that case, on the day of the concert, you have to enjoy my perfect performance from the audience!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Alright, I'll be there.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'll be watching you from the audience, supporting you. I'll be your most loyal spectator no matter what.
Echo's eyes sparkle with joy as she gives you an enthusiastic thumbs up.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: You made a promise. Don't go missing on that day!
